facts.raw_span: A young girl initially came under care at age 4 years
developed an irregular brown-black patch on her left lateral ankle, measuring 3.6 × 3 cm
triangular hyperpigmented, asymptomatic patch consisting of confluent mottled black and brown macules and several satellite lesions
slow but progressive growth of the hyperpigmented patch, which had increased to 5.5 × 5-cm
two discrete areas of regression were noted
discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas with gray-brown structureless areas and a negative pigment network were observed
No induration was palpated except at the previous biopsy site
Shows a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction consistent with an atypical compound nevus
Shows atypical nevus with areas of dermal fibrosis
Score: -7.1 (where scores from -16.7 to -2.1 are consistent with a benign nevus)
A large, dark brown patch consisting of coalescing macules and satellite lesions
The patch shows areas of regression on the medial and left upper borders

concepts.why: The patient developed a hyperpigmented patch on her left lateral ankle at a young age, which is consistent with a congenital melanocytic nevus, and histopathology results show a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction.

The patient's nevus shows atypical features, including large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, and areas of dermal fibrosis, which are consistent with an atypical nevus.
The patient has a hyperpigmented patch on her left lateral ankle, which is consistent with a melanocytic nevus, and the patch shows characteristics of a melanocytic proliferation.
The patient's nevus has a score of -7.1 on the Myriad myPath test, which is consistent with a benign nevus.
The patient's nevus shows areas of regression, which is consistent with a nevus that is undergoing regression.
The patient's nevus shows atypical features, including large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, which are consistent with an atypical compound nevus.
It explains the discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas observed on dermoscopy.

rationales.F02: The presence of a brown-black patch is more typical of congenital melanocytic nevi and atypical nevi.
rationales.F05: The presence of regression is highly suggestive of a nevus with regression.
rationales.F08: The histopathology showing a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes is highly suggestive of an atypical compound nevus.
rationales.F10: The gene expression testing score is consistent with a benign nevus, making it less likely to be an atypical nevus or melanocytic nevus.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, along with areas of dermal fibrosis and regression, supports the diagnosis of Atypical Compound Nevus, which is a more specific entity than Congenital Melanocytic Nevus.
